deep.reconstruction:
This page belongs to Grothendieck's 1953 drafting of a Banach-space Fredholm theory, the material that became 'Produits tensoriels topologiques et espaces nucléaires' (Mem. AMS 16, 1955, ch. II) and 'La théorie de Fredholm' (Bull. SMF 84, 1956).

Setting. 'Applications/opérateurs de Fredholm' here means nuclear (trace-class) maps. The quantity ||·||_1 is the nuclear (trace) norm. The coefficients α_n(u_1,…,u_n) are the multilinear Fredholm coefficients, with α_n(u) the coefficients of det(1+zu) = Σ α_n(u) z^n.

Previous page. Proposition 3 shows that u_1∧…∧u_n is nuclear on the completed exterior power Λ^n E, with ||u_1∧…∧u_n||_1 ≤ (1/n!) Π||u_i||_1 (formula 13). The proof checks rank-one maps and uses continuity. The corollary there gives α_n(u) = Tr(Λ^n u) (formula 14).

This page.
- Top: completes that argument. Combined with (13) it yields Corollary 2: |α_n(u_1,…,u_n)| ≤ (1/n!) ||u_1||_1 … ||u_n||_1 (formula 15), boxed in red. This is the Banach-space form of the classical Fredholm/Carleman bound |α_n(u)| ≤ ||u||_1^n / n!, which guarantees that det(1+zu) is entire. A parenthetical remark says it also follows from a result in Chap. I, §1, N°2.
- Corollary 3 (Hilbert space E):
  - For u trace class, ||Λ^n u||_1 = α_n(|u|) = α_n(√(u*u)) (formula 16).
  - For u Hilbert–Schmidt, ||Λ^n u||_2 = √(α_n(u*u)) (formula 17).
  - In modern terms both say that the singular values of Λ^n u are the products s_{i1}⋯s_{in}, i_1<…<i_n. Hence ||Λ^n u||_1 = e_n(s_1, s_2, …) and ||Λ^n u||_2² = e_n(s_1², s_2², …), where e_n is the elementary symmetric function.
- Proof of (16): ||Λ^n u||_1 = Tr((Λ^n u)*(Λ^n u))^{1/2} (N°1, formula 22). Since Λ^n is multiplicative and *-preserving, ((Λ^n u)*Λ^n u)^{1/2} = Λ^n((u*u)^{1/2}). Apply (14).
- Proof of (17): after several crossed-out attempts, he argues as follows. u Hilbert–Schmidt implies u*u is trace class (N°1, th. 4). So Λ^n(u*u) = (Λ^n u)*(Λ^n u) is trace class, hence Λ^n u is Hilbert–Schmidt. Then ||Λ^n u||_2² = Tr Λ^n(u*u) = α_n(u*u).

Purpose. These identities feed the next page:
- |α_n(u)| ≤ α_n(|u|), proved as |Tr Λ^n u| ≤ ||Λ^n u||_1;
- |det(1+u)| ≤ det(1+|u|);
- a stated theorem det(1+u) = Π(1+λ_i) and Tr u = Σλ_i for trace-class operators on Hilbert space. That is Lidskii's theorem; its proof is crossed out there.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The bound (15) depends on the 1/n! normalisation of u_1∧…∧u_n fixed on the previous page (formula 8). Under that convention α_n(u) = Tr Λ^n u is consistent with the classical Fredholm series.

Minor gap: the identity ((Λ^n u)*(Λ^n u))^{1/2} = Λ^n((u*u)^{1/2}) on the completed Hilbert exterior power needs Λ^n to be a *-homomorphism compatible with the functional calculus. It is, but this is only asserted.
The (17) argument went through several crossed-out versions. The final version is correct: u Hilbert–Schmidt ⇒ u*u trace class ⇒ Λ^n u Hilbert–Schmidt.

ideas.what: Nuclear-norm bound for exterior products and Fredholm coefficients in Banach spaces: |α_n(u_1,…,u_n)| ≤ (1/n!) Π||u_i||_1
ideas.modern_name: Fredholm–Carleman type estimate; Grothendieck's Fredholm theory for nuclear operators
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fredholm (1903) for integral kernels; Grothendieck (1955/56) for nuclear operators on Banach spaces
ideas.where_published: Produits tensoriels topologiques (Mem. AMS 16, 1955), ch. II; La théorie de Fredholm (Bull. SMF 84, 1956)

ideas.what: Fredholm coefficients as traces of exterior powers: α_n(u) = Tr Λ^n u
ideas.modern_name: Determinant via traces of exterior powers (Simon, Trace Ideals, ch. 3)

ideas.what: Hilbert-space identities ||Λ^n u||_1 = α_n(|u|) and ||Λ^n u||_2² = α_n(u*u), i.e. the singular values of Λ^n u are products of the singular values of u
ideas.modern_name: Singular values of antisymmetric tensor powers; ||Λ^n u||_1 = e_n(s(u))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore / Weyl–Horn circle; standard in Simon's Trace Ideals and Gohberg–Krein
ideas.where_published: possibly La théorie de Fredholm (1956), Hilbert-space section

missed.claim: This page builds the tools for the next page, which states det(1+u) = Π(1+λ_i) and Tr u = Σλ_i for all trace-class operators on Hilbert space, i.e. Lidskii's theorem (1959), and then crosses out the proof. This documents an attempted 1953 proof of the Hilbert-space trace formula, six years before Lidskii, apparently abandoned. Grothendieck's published version only covers nuclear operators of order 2/3 on Banach spaces.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically relevant to the priority story of Lidskii's theorem and to why Grothendieck restricted to order 2/3. It is not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The results on this page are standard estimates that Grothendieck published (or that are folklore). Interest lies only in the adjacent, abandoned attempt at the Hilbert-space Lidskii formula, which is not on this page itself.
transcription_corrections: In (15) the norms on the right are trace/nuclear norms ||u_i||_1, per the 'conditions précédentes' and (13).
In Corollary 3 the exterior power is written with a hat, \hat{Λ}^n u (completed exterior power), not plain Λ^n.
Corollary 3 opening reads roughly 'Soit u un op. de Fredholm dans un espace de Hilbert E … on a', not 'α = α_n Λ^n'.
In (16) the final '= α_n(√(u*u))' is a red-ink addition, and an earlier argument of α_n is crossed out.
In the proof of (16), '(N° 1, formule (22))' refers to ||v||_1 = Tr (v*v)^{1/2}. The last parenthetical before the crossed-out passage is 'compte tenu de (14)'.
Final line: '(formule (14), d'où (17))' is a marginal remark at line end.
